seen_animation: A line-drawn crab faces the viewer between grey wavy scenery lines: oval carapace, two raised claws on long arms, four short leg strokes below, and two short eyestalks ending in small diamonds. Frames 1-7 hold this pose with only small redraw shimmer in the claw strokes. In frame 8 both eyestalks tip outward and down toward the carapace edge. In frame 9 the stalks are gone and the two diamond eyes lie flat inside the top of the carapace with short dashes beside them. In frame 10 the stalks are rising again, tilted outward, and by frame 11 they are upright again. Frames 11-16 hold the upright pose with slight claw shimmer. The body, claws and legs do not travel.
seen_film: A pale ghost crab sits facing the camera on sand, slightly left of centre, with its large claw hanging down at front-left and the smaller claw at right, legs spread to both sides. Frames 1-7 it is still, with upright eyestalks and small mouthpart movement. In frame 8 the eyestalks fold down and outward, in frame 9 they lie flat against the carapace, in frame 10 they are coming back up (blurred), and from frame 11 to 16 they are upright again while the crab stays in place.
named_subject: a crab (ghost crab) folding its eyestalks down and raising them again
evidence: The single event in the film, the eyestalk fold and return, happens on the same frames in the animation: stalks begin tipping in frame 8 (film frame 8), are flat on the carapace in frame 9 (film frame 9), are rising in frame 10 (film frame 10), and are upright in frame 11 (film frame 11). Frames 1-7 and 11-16 hold still in both. The crab body stays centred in the same region of the frame as the film crab across all 16 frames, and claws, legs and carapace keep the doodle's construction throughout. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: In frames 8 and 10 the left eye diamond lands directly on the left claw-arm line, so the folding stalk and the arm overlap and the eye is hard to read as a separate part mid-fold.
closes_when: In frames 8 and 10 the left eyestalk swings down along a path inside the arm (closer to the carapace centre) so its diamond stays visibly clear of the left claw-arm stroke, mirroring the right eye.
protect: The fold timing on frames 8-9-10-11 matching the film; the still hold in frames 1-7 and 11-16; the fixed body position; the doodle's carapace outline with the left-side break, the two-stroke-pair legs, and the hooked claw shapes; the diamond-on-a-stick eye style that suits the doodle's line language.
identity_gap: The doodle has no eyestalks, so the added stick-and-diamond eyes are new parts, but they are drawn in the same thin single-stroke style and the rest of the crab matches the doodle closely.
